clips.stepText: Turning away from wrongdoing is what repenting means. Picture the relief when you find a missing purse after searching. Luke puts that feeling beside a person returning. Look for repeated moments of celebration, including what the father says to the older son.

clips.stepText: Focus on what someone does when there is a need. Picture stopping to help a pupil who fell when others kept walking. At the end Jesus changes the focus of the question. Look at who showed mercy through action.

clips.stepText: Put both parts of the story side by side. Picture the same two people at the beginning and at the end of a play. Here their situations change sharply. Check what Abraham says about the warnings the brothers already have.

clips.stepText: The plan sounds good until you ask what the man leaves out. Picture counting savings for years you assume you will have. His time is cut short in the story. Look at the question God asks about the things he has prepared.

clips.mathToSpeechText: Why does she keep going back? Think of a pupil who follows up on a request that was ignored. The repeated visits give you the point. Notice how the judge finally answers and what Jesus asks us about God.

clips.stepText: A publican was a tax collector. Picture two pupils explaining themselves to a teacher. One brags and the other asks for help. Listen for the difference in the prayers. It prepares you for Jesus’ judgment at the end.

clips.stepText: Go back to the road and watch what each traveller does. Try answering before you read the last verse. Then see whether Jesus’ closing question directs you to the same person you picked.

clips.stepText: Check for the person who stops and takes responsibility. The priest keeps going. The Levite leaves too. The innkeeper enters after the man has been brought in. Now look at who notices the need and begins to help.

clips.stepText: Look at what makes the judge finally respond. That helps you sort the options. Two stories here involve prayer. The one you want uses a woman’s repeated visits to make its point about keeping on.
